title: Session affinity loadbook and noise conditioning
body:
Purpose:
This note captures a lightweight, repeatable playbook for throughput benchmarking runs that explicitly model session affinity and controlled noise-conditioning. The aim is to make fanout/multi-session benchmarks closer to realistic production traffic where per-session KV caches, user-level priming, and request affinity change throughput and tail latency behavior.

Scope and motivation:
- Existing loadbooks assume stateless, iid single-request arrivals. For LLM inference the per-session KV cache and priming tokens materially affect per-token compute and memory pressure.
- We need an experiment harness that:
  * Reproduces affinity patterns (sticky sessions, short-lived sessions, high-churn sessions)
  * Provides knobs to inject controlled noise (timing jitter, token-length variability, model-variant mix)
  * Ensures RNG and seed hygiene so runs are comparable across weeks and hardware

Key definitions used in this playbook:
- Session affinity: a client mapping where multiple requests share a session id and therefore share KV cache state on the serving node.
- Priming window: tokens sent in the first request(s) of a session that populate the KV cache.
- Noise conditioning: intentional injection of variability (arrival jitter, payload entropy, cold-start fraction) to simulate production non-ideality.
- Anchor run: a long, deterministic run used as a baseline comparing all variants.

Principles:
1) Isolate variables: change only one axis per experiment (affinity mode, priming length, jitter profile).
2) Repeatability: each experiment must have an anchor seed and a documented seed hygiene policy.
3) Observability-first: capture token-level compute, GPU occupancy, KV cache hit rate, per-request trace ids, and client-side timestamps.
4) Graceful ramp: use a 3-stage warmup (fast-fill priming, paced ramp, steady anchor) to avoid thermal and scheduler-induced discontinuities.

Affinity modes to include in the harness:
- sticky-long: 1k sessions, average session lifetime 100 requests (high KV reuse).
- sticky-short: 10k sessions, average lifetime 5 requests (medium KV reuse).
- stateless: each request unique session id (no reuse).
- churned: sessions open and close rapidly with sporadic bursts (models connection churn).

Warmup and priming recipe (recommended default):
1) Priming phase (3 minutes): create N sessions and send a single priming request with a 128-token prompt for each session. Purpose: populate on-device caches and warm kernels.
2) Ramp phase (6 minutes): linearly increase request rate to target throughput while maintaining session mix. Interleave priming requests at a 5% rate to simulate new users.
3) Anchor steady-state (15–30 minutes): fixed target concurrency and request profile. Capture full telemetry.
Notes: scale durations up for multi-GPU experiments; thermal effects can require longer priming (10–15m) on heterogeneous fleets.

Noise conditioning knobs (examples):
- timing_jitter: distribution choices {none, gaussian(sd=5ms), pareto(alpha=1.5)}
- payload_variability: fraction of requests following long-tail length distribution (p=0.1 length~U[512,1024])
- cold_fraction: percent of requests that are intentionally sent as first-request-for-session (default 5%)
- model_mix: list of model aliases with weights, used to exercise quantized vs float paths
- client_clock_skew: simulate client timestamp drift for tracing-based latency computation

RNG and seed hygiene:
- Global seed: each named experiment gets a UUID and a numeric anchor seed. Both must be logged in run metadata.
- Session assignment: deterministically map session_id -> RNG stream derived from anchor seed using HMAC(session_id, seed) so sessions are consistently recreated across runs.
- Request perturbations (jitter, token sampling): use dedicated substreams derived from the global seed to avoid cross-correlation.
- Immutable configs: store the exact config (including seed) with run artifacts; when rerunning, use exact seeds unless intentionally testing variance.

Sample loadgen configuration (YAML-like example for readability):
---
name: churned-high-throughput
anchor_seed: 20250220-83
clients: 200
session_pool: 10000
affinity_mode: churned
priming:
  priming_tokens: 96
  priming_rate_pct: 5
timing_jitter: gaussian(sd_ms=10)
payload_profile:
  long_tail_fraction: 0.12
  median_tokens: 64
model_mix:
  rwd-llama-70b-q4: 0.8
  rwd-llama-70b-fp16: 0.2
run_schedule:
  priming_mins: 3
  ramp_mins: 8
  steady_mins: 20
observability: [token_time_ms, gpu_util, nvtx, kv_hit_rate, req_trace]
---

Metrics to capture (minimum):
- per-token latency distributions (p50,p90,p95,p99,p99.9)
- per-request end-to-end latency (client->server->client)
- GPU occupancy / SM utilization sampled at 1s granularity
- KV cache hit/miss ratio by session age bucket
- Queue lengths, executor saturation, and backpressure signals
- Retry and error counts, broken down by model variant and session age

Analysis recipes:
- Compare sticky-long vs stateless: focus on token-averaged compute and memory pressure; expect lower per-token latency in sticky-long due to KV reuse, but watch for hot-spotting on a subset of GPUs.
- Noise sensitivity sweep: run the same anchor with incrementally increasing timing_jitter and cold_fraction to measure slope of p99 increase.
- Seed perturbation test: rerun anchor with 3 different seeds and compute variance decomposition (within-seed vs across-seed). High across-seed variance indicates workload nondeterminism or fragile priming.

Runbook (quick checklist before an anchor run):
- [ ] Confirm hardware pool and model variants pinned in run manifest.
- [ ] Upload and lock loadgen config with anchor_seed in artifact store.
- [ ] Start background telemetry collectors (nvprof/rocprof, p99-trace-sampler, kv-prober).
- [ ] Execute priming phase, then verify KV hit rate increases by >20% vs cold baseline.
- [ ] Verify cluster thermal profile stable (GPU temps, clock frequency).
- [ ] Run anchor steady-state and collect logs.
- [ ] Immediately snapshot run metadata and manifest (seeds, config, git commit).

Troubleshooting notes (common failure modes):
- Symptom: sudden drop in throughput after 10m in sticky-long mode.
  Cause: KV hot-spotting overloading a subset of executors; TTL-based eviction causing churn.
  Mitigation: broaden session hashing, increase cache size or add prefetching of adjacent KV pages.

- Symptom: high p99 variance between runs with same seed.
  Cause: asynchronous background maintenance (checkpointing, GC) or non-deterministic scheduling.
  Mitigation: schedule maintenance windows, isolate GPU hosts, increase warmup to allow steady-state scheduler to settle.

Open questions / experiments to prioritize:
- Impact of session sharding strategies on hot-spot formation at >2k sessions/GPU.
- Does targeted prefetch of likely-Attention keys reduce variance more than increasing global cache?
- Quantify model-mix elasticity: how small a float-fp16 slice causes perf cliff under high occupancy?

Appendix: minimal telemetry field spec (CSV-friendly):
run_id,anchor_seed,timestamp_ms,client_ts_ms,session_id,request_id,model_alias,request_tokens,response_tokens,token_ms,gpu_util_pct,kv_hit,trace_id,error_code

Notes to self: this document is intentionally prescriptive but lightweight — aim to convert into a runnable benchmark manifest and a reusable loadgen template in the bench-harness repo.
